searchText: How does the cross link committee determine what the root of the shard is that they are attesting to? My understanding is that they ask the persistent committee because surely they aren't executing the shard -- right? The crosslink committee syncs the shard since the latest crosslink and executes the fork choice rule to find the head. In phase 0, there is no state execution so it is just the fork choice on the data chain. In phase 2, the expectation is to run the state transitions in the state-less EE model, this can be done simply via the data contained in the blocks (merkle state witnesses are embedded) and thus no full state sync has to occur. So they _do_ execute the actual shard transitions When crosslinking, they are making a claim on the availability and validity of the data proof of custody games handle the availability portion. fraud proofs will handle validity **will_vill** Is there any approximated idea yet or study of how long a simple light sync should take - lets say a sync on the data without thinking of stateless execution overhead? Since there is a shuffling on the crosslink committee for each epoch and a 1 epoch lookahead - curious how this affects the extreme cases such as approaching MAX_EPOCHS_PER_CROSSLINK **vbuterin** So the current light client protocol uses persistent committees, not crosslink committees **will_vill** So time to download each block assuming it is at its max data capacity, run the fork-choice related data and sync to that as well (historic attestations that are also off-chain), initial networking overhead and run verification over the fork choice. Assuming worst possible scenario, this would be 64 * 64 * 2 slots, right? **will_vill** Yeah - specifically related to a sync by a crosslink committee validator who is syncing to the designated shard
